body.title: SQL Server Incremental Batch Sync Between Instances
body.description: Move only what changed between two SQL Server instances, and never lose track of where the last run left off. This blueprint reads a watermark from Kestra's KV Store, pulls every row updated since that point from a source table, bulk-inserts the delta into a destination instance using chunked JDBC batch operations, then advances the watermark only after the load commits. A failed run leaves the watermark untouched, so the next execution retries the exact same window instead of skipping rows or double-loading them. ## How it works 1. `read_watermark` (`io.kestra.plugin.core.kv.Get`) reads the `orders_sync_watermark` key from the namespace KV Store. On the first run, `errorOnMissing: false` lets the flow fall through to the epoch (`1900-01-01T00:00:00`). 2. `extract_since_watermark` (`io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Query`) selects every row from `dbo.orders` where `updated_at` is greater than the watermark, binding it as a `:watermark` prepared-statement parameter, and stores the result set with `fetchType: STORE`. 3. `bulk_load` (`io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Batch`) reads that stored file and bulk-inserts it into `dbo.orders_reporting` on the destination instance, in chunks of 1,000 rows per JDBC batch call. 4. `compute_new_watermark` (`io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Query`) re-reads the maximum `updated_at` committed on the source for the same window, with `fetchType: FETCH_ONE`. 5. `advance_watermark` (`io.kestra.plugin.core.kv.Set`) writes that value back to `orders_sync_watermark`, but only after `bulk_load` has already succeeded, so a mid-batch failure never advances the watermark past what was actually committed downstream. 6. `notify` (`io.kestra.plugin.slack.notifications.SlackIncomingWebhook`) confirms the row count and new watermark; the `errors` block posts a separate Slack alert on failure. Source and destination credentials are set individually on each `Query` and `Batch` task, so the same flow can point at two different SQL Server instances. ## What you get - An idempotent incremental sync: reruns after a failure never skip or duplicate rows, because the watermark only advances on success. - Chunked bulk inserts (1,000 rows per JDBC batch) instead of row-by-row `INSERT` statements. - Watermark state tracked in the KV Store, with no external state table required. - Slack confirmation on success and a distinct Slack alert on failure. ## Who it's for - Data engineers replicating operational tables between SQL Server instances or into a reporting database. - Platform teams migrating off SSIS packages and SQL Server Agent jobs for cross-instance data movement. - Teams who need resumable, chunked bulk loads without standing up a full CDC pipeline. ## Why orchestrate this with Kestra SQL Server Agent can run a stored procedure on a schedule, but it has no built-in concept of a portable watermark, no chunked bulk-insert primitive across two different instances, and no way to skip a Slack alert on success while still alerting on failure. Kestra adds all of that: the KV Store tracks state across runs, `io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Batch` chunks the insert with automatic retry and resume behavior, and the `errors` block guarantees a failed run is never silent. ## Prerequisites - A source SQL Server database with a `dbo.orders` table containing an `updated_at` column suitable as a watermark. - A destination SQL Server database with a `dbo.orders_reporting` table matching the selected columns. - A Slack incoming webhook for notifications. ### Secrets - `SQLSERVER_SOURCE_URL`: JDBC URL for the source instance, for example `jdbc:sqlserver://source-host:1433;trustServerCertificate=true`. - `SQLSERVER_SOURCE_USERNAME` / `SQLSERVER_SOURCE_PASSWORD`: credentials for the source instance. - `SQLSERVER_DEST_URL`: JDBC URL for the destination instance. - `SQLSERVER_DEST_USERNAME` / `SQLSERVER_DEST_PASSWORD`: credentials for the destination instance. - `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`: Slack incoming webhook URL. ## Quick start 1. Add the secrets above to your Kestra namespace. 2. Confirm the source `dbo.orders` table and destination `dbo.orders_reporting` table exist with matching columns. 3. Run the flow once manually to seed the watermark, then enable the hourly `Schedule` trigger. 4. Check the KV Store for the `orders_sync_watermark` key after each run to confirm it advances. ## How to extend - Swap `table` for an explicit `sql` INSERT statement on `Batch` if the source and destination column order differs. - Replace the `Schedule` trigger with a `Flow` trigger so the sync fires the moment an upstream load finishes. - Add a row-count `If` check after `bulk_load` to branch on an unexpectedly large or small batch before advancing the watermark. - Chain a Snowflake or dbt load after `bulk_load` for a full cross-database ETL pattern. ## Links - Plugin docs: https://kestra.io/plugins/plugin-jdbc-sqlserver - SQL Server orchestration with Kestra: https://kestra.io/orchestration/sql-server
body.shortDescription: Extract changed rows from a source SQL Server table since the last KV-tracked watermark and bulk-insert them into a destination instance with chunked JDBC batches.
body.metaTitle: SQL Server Incremental Batch Sync with Kestra
body.metaDescription: Orchestrate incremental SQL Server to SQL Server sync with Kestra. Extract changed rows since a watermark and bulk-insert them with chunked, resumable JDBC batches.
body.flow:
id: sql-server-incremental-batch-sync
namespace: company.team
description: |
  Extract only the rows changed since the last watermark from a source SQL Server table,
  then bulk-insert them into a destination SQL Server instance using chunked JDBC batch
  inserts. The watermark is read from and written to the KV Store, so a rerun after a
  partial failure resumes from the last committed load instead of skipping or duplicating rows.

triggers:
  - id: hourly
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Schedule
    description: Run the incremental sync hourly. Adjust or disable as needed.
    cron: "0 * * * *"
    disabled: true

tasks:
  - id: read_watermark
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.kv.Get
    description: Read the last committed watermark; falls through to the epoch on first run.
    key: orders_sync_watermark
    errorOnMissing: false

  - id: extract_since_watermark
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Query
    description: Pull only the rows changed since the last watermark from the source
      instance.
    url: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_URL') }}"
    username: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_USERNAME') }}"
    password: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_PASSWORD') }}"
    trustServerCertificate: true
    sql: |
      SELECT order_id, customer_id, status, total, updated_at
      FROM dbo.orders
      WHERE updated_at > :watermark
      ORDER BY updated_at ASC;
    parameters:
      watermark: "{{ outputs.read_watermark.value ?? '1900-01-01T00:00:00' }}"
    fetchType: STORE

  - id: bulk_load
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Batch
    description: Bulk-insert the extracted rows into the destination instance in
      chunks of 1,000.
    url: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_DEST_URL') }}"
    username: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_DEST_USERNAME') }}"
    password: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_DEST_PASSWORD') }}"
    trustServerCertificate: true
    from: "{{ outputs.extract_since_watermark.uri }}"
    table: dbo.orders_reporting
    chunk: 1000

  - id: compute_new_watermark
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.sqlserver.Query
    description: Read back the latest committed updated_at, reached only once the
      bulk load succeeds.
    url: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_URL') }}"
    username: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_USERNAME') }}"
    password: "{{ secret('SQLSERVER_SOURCE_PASSWORD') }}"
    trustServerCertificate: true
    sql: |
      SELECT MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at
      FROM dbo.orders
      WHERE updated_at > :watermark;
    parameters:
      watermark: "{{ outputs.read_watermark.value ?? '1900-01-01T00:00:00' }}"
    fetchType: FETCH_ONE

  - id: advance_watermark
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.kv.Set
    description: Persist the new watermark only after the destination load has committed.
    key: orders_sync_watermark
    value: "{{ outputs.compute_new_watermark.row.max_updated_at ??
      (outputs.read_watermark.value ?? '1900-01-01T00:00:00') }}"

  - id: notify
    type: io.kestra.plugin.slack.notifications.SlackIncomingWebhook
    description: Confirm the sync completed with the row count and the new watermark.
    url: "{{ secret('SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL') }}"
    payload: |
      {
        "text": "SQL Server incremental sync loaded {{ outputs.bulk_load.updatedCount }} rows. Watermark advanced to {{ outputs.advance_watermark.value }}."
      }

errors:
  - id: alert_on_failure
    type: io.kestra.plugin.slack.notifications.SlackIncomingWebhook
    description: Alert Slack if extraction or the bulk load fails; the watermark is
      not advanced so the next run retries the same window.
    url: "{{ secret('SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL') }}"
    payload: |
      {
        "text": "SQL Server incremental sync failed and did not advance the watermark (execution {{ execution.id }})."
      }
